items.d: Chunyang Palace is the largest Taoist temple in the ancient city of Datong. The temple is divided into two sections: the western section is a garden, and the eastern section has three courtyards.

Main meeting point for climbers and boulderers. You can rent and buy equipment, meet fellow climbers over a cup of coffee, or book a climbing activity with Jerry, the owner (₹1000, usually in the morning).
Fathabad Garden is a historical Persian garden located near Kerman.
Local history museum administered by the museum in Sisimiut.
The most important architectural building in San Telmo and one of the most important in the city. It has 200 years of history. You only visit by guided tour which takes about an hour.

This is a centre for rehabilitated horses located on the Sheikh's working farm. Visitors can lease a horse, sign up for riding lessons, or simply wander around the grounds and mingle with the peacocks in the shade.
Small-group tour operator offering Northern Lights excursions, snowmobile safaris, husky tours, reindeer experiences, hiking and national park tours.
Observation point with nice view of the dam.Tourism information centre with a small exhibition inside.Curios sold outside.

items.d: Barili's paintings collected from all over the world. Barili was one of the well known painters in the world in 19th century.

An open air museum and Gesamtkunstwerk, created by the local artist Anders Åberg. The site features an agricultural museum, art museums, a bureaucracy museum, a coastal museum, an accordion museum, a Chinese pavilion, a subway,…
The shows are fun, energetic and exciting and include a range of circus disciplines. The ticket price helps support the NGO school which works with disadvantaged children and teenagers.

Smaller church beside the Church of the Transfiguration. A winter church, built in 17-18th century, it looks like a smaller and more austere variant of the summer church, with 9 domes and cramped interiors.
Hike to Knivskjellodden, the northernmost point of mainland Norway: 1.5 km more to the north than Nordkapp and with a good view to there. The track is marked with red T's.
This is the house where Simon Bolivar stayed during the Congress of Angostura. With a lush tropical garden. Entrance free.
This centennial Ficus tree is honored in the official municipal hymn of Florianópolis.
The building, 18th or beginning of 19th century, stands out with a brick-built dome and contrasts from the rest of Quba's architecture.

Formerly the Sarawak State Mosque, Kuching's main mosque. Later it was re-designated as the Kuching Divisional Mosque. It was built in 1968 on a site that had been used for a wooden mosque as early as 1852.
At Nørreskiftegaard near Ballen, you can try horse riding.
The former residence of the colonial governor. The building was designed and built in Glasgow and shipped over in pieces. The museum concentrates on the history of Calabar, the region and slavery.
This Roman Catholic church is opposite the main building of the University of Munich (LMU Munich). It's in Romanesque style, and features the second-largest altar fresco in the world.
Svetozar Miletić (1826-1901) was the most prominent political leader of the Serbian people during the Habsburg Monarchy. He was a lawyer, journalist, author, politician, mayor of Novi Sad.

It is the site of one of the earliest discoveries of human habitation in Vietnam. Excavated in 1966, the cave revealed human graves, stone axes, pointed bone spears, oyster shell knives, and tools for grinding dating back 7,500…
A simply beautiful place inside Yankari resort. The spring is clear a bit warm with a temperature that is constant great place for water games and swimming.

This is the birthplace of Sheikha Mozah (the second wife of Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the former Emir of Qatar). Although the house has not been maintained, it is a good example of traditional Qatari architecture.

This museum is made up of a cluster of houses with furnishings and displays appropriate to an Omani house between 1950 and 1970, i.e. before the accession of Sultan Qaboos. There is also a small modern art gallery.
Historical performance venue, including international dance and opera, worth a visit even if just from its outside.
The mosque was built in the 1940s on the site of earlier mosques, and while not particularly old was built with traditional construction of coral and rock with a baked mud roof.

A very small but intricate domed pavilion, known for being the only surviving example of Almoravid religious architecture (early 12th century) in Marrakech.
Beautiful mosque. Entrance only with long trousers. Next door is the grand Isatay and Makhambet Square with a noble statue of these guys on horseback.
